suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is read without optional chaining, and mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined when evt.destinationCalendar is null or empty. WHY: any Google Meet booking where neither the organizer nor the event type has a destination calendar throws a TypeError, and booking creation fails. The old code used `?.`. HOW: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: references for non-calendar results (video) now get `credentialId: undefined`, where they used to get result.credentialId. WHY: handleCancelBooking only deletes video meetings when the video reference has a credentialId, so Zoom/Daily meetings are no longer deleted on cancel. HOW: keep result.credentialId for every result type.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the fallback only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, but it then searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, so it never matches a real calendar. WHY: the calendar id becomes undefined, which drops the old fallback to destinationCalendar.externalId and sends updates for legacy references to the wrong calendar or makes them fail. HOW: fall back to the first destination calendar's externalId.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the deleteEvent fallback searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it always returns undefined. WHY: for references without externalCalendarId, the destination calendar fallback is lost and the delete falls back to the default calendar. If the event lives in a different calendar, it is left behind. HOW: use `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, so `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing. WHY: in collective events where the first host has no destination calendar, the other hosts' calendars are silently dropped, which is the case this PR is supposed to fix. HOW: default to `[]` instead of null.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: createEvent always uses destinationCalendar[0].externalId. createAllCalendarEvents now calls it once per host credential, so every host's Office365 credential gets the first host's calendar id. WHY: a second collective host using Office365 posts to `/me/calendars/<host1-calendar-id>/events`, which does not exist in their account, so their event creation fails. HOW: pick the destination entry whose credentialId matches this credential, as GoogleCalendarService does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the recurring-series branch, which deletes the events of all updatedBookings for every user calendar credential, now sits inside the per-reference loop. WHY: with multiple calendar references, the same recurring events get one delete call per reference, which causes duplicate API calls and 404/410 errors. HOW: move the recurring deletion out of the reference loop so it runs once.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the slug condition was flipped from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`. WHY: with billing enabled, the slug is set right away and also stored as requestedSlug, and with billing disabled, organizations are created with no slug. HOW: restore the negation.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the catch block turns the plain Error thrown for an empty or invalid dynamicUserList into a generic 500 'Unable to load users'. WHY: a client input error comes back as a server error with its message hidden. HOW: throw `new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, ... })` directly for the validation failure.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` comes from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so it is `undefined` when there is no destination calendar. Callers now pass `[]` or `null` in that case. A Google Meet booking without a destination calendar then throws a TypeError on `.integration` instead of falling back to Cal Video.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `find` fallback only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but it searches for a calendar whose `externalId` equals that same falsy value. It therefore never returns the event's destination calendar, and the update goes out with an undefined calendarId instead of the destination calendar used before this PR.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, `destinationCalendar` is set to `null`. The following `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then does nothing, so collective team members' calendars are silently discarded. Initializing it to an empty array keeps them.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When there is no destination calendar, handleNewBooking now passes `destinationCalendar: null` and other callers pass `[]`. `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` then leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined, so reading `.integration` throws a TypeError. Every Google Meet booking without a destination calendar fails instead of falling back to Cal Video; using `?.integration` keeps the old fallback.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When evt.destinationCalendar is null or [] (handleNewBooking sets null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined. `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` then throws a TypeError for every Google Meet booking. This breaks booking creation in the very case the Cal Video fallback is meant to handle.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `destinationCalendar` is now an array, and when it is null or empty (handleNewBooking passes null if no event-type or organizer calendar is set), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined. The old code read `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which handled null. The new code reads `.integration` on undefined, so every such booking throws a TypeError in EventManager.create. The fix is optional chaining on `mainHostDestinationCalendar`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but it searches `destinationCalendar` for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` using that same falsy value. The search never matches, so `selectedCalendar` is undefined. Before this change, the code fell back to the destination calendar's externalId.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new catch block in loadUsers copies `error.message` from `PrismaClientKnownRequestError` into a 400 HttpError, which this public, unauthenticated booking endpoint sends back to the caller. Prisma error messages can include model, field and constraint names and query details, which exposes internal database structure. Log the Prisma error on the server and return a generic message to the client.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: For COLLECTIVE events, every team member's full DestinationCalendar row (credentialId, externalId, userId) is now pushed into `evt.destinationCalendar`. `evt` is spread into the webhook payload, so other members' calendar IDs (often email addresses) and their credential IDs are sent to the webhook subscriber. Keep the team members' calendars off `evt`, for example by passing them to EventManager separately, or remove the field before building the payload.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The old code set `slug` only when team billing was disabled. The rewrite sets it only when billing is enabled, the same condition as `requestedSlug`. With billing enabled, orgs now get a final slug before payment or verification. With billing disabled, they get no slug at all.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The else branch runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, yet it looks for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`. That can never match a real calendar, so the destination calendar fallback is dead code and `selectedCalendar` is always undefined. The same expression appears in deleteEvent (lines 315-317). The fallback should pick the destination calendar that belongs to this credential, or the main host's calendar.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The old code used `result.credentialId` for non-calendar (video) results. The new ternary returns `undefined` for them, so video references are stored without the credential that created the meeting. Later updates and deletes of those meetings can no longer find the right credential.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `destinationCalendar` falls back to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one. In that case `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing, and the destination calendars of the other collective hosts are thrown away. Initializing to an empty array keeps those team calendars.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses `&&` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, and isTeamAdmin already matches ADMIN or OWNER roles, so the check passes only for OWNERs. WHY: Team ADMINs who are not the organizer or an attendee get FORBIDDEN, even though the variable name says admins should be allowed. HOW: Use `||`, or just call isTeamAdmin, which already covers owners.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails gets the raw `guests` input instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`. WHY: An already-existing attendee who appears in the submitted list is treated as a new guest and gets a 'new booking scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notice. HOW: Pass `uniqueGuests`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: EventManager is built from the caller's (ctx.user) credentials, but updateCalendarAttendees updates the booking references that live in the organizer's calendar. WHY: When an attendee or team owner adds guests, the calendar update runs with credentials that don't own those events, so the organizer's calendar event never gets the new attendees, or the update throws. HOW: Build EventManager from booking.user and that user's credentials, as other booking handlers do.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: updateCalendarAttendees runs after attendees are already saved to the database, and it is not wrapped in error handling. WHY: If the calendar provider call fails, the client gets an error but the guests stay saved without emails, and a retry is rejected with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. HOW: Wrap the calendar update in try/catch and log the error so emails still go out and the mutation reports success.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Blacklist entries are lowercased, but each guest email is compared with its original casing. WHY: Submitting a blacklisted address with any uppercase letter (e.g. `Bad@x.com`) gets past BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and the address is added and emailed. HOW: Lowercase the guest before comparing it to the blacklist and to existing attendees.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The server schema accepts duplicate emails in `guests`, and the handler only removes guests that are already attendees, not repeats within the input. WHY: A direct API call with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows via createMany, because the uniqueness check exists only on the client. HOW: Add a refine that rejects duplicates (or dedupe with a Set in the handler).

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `guests` has no maximum length, and any booking attendee is allowed to call the mutation. WHY: An authenticated attendee can submit thousands of arbitrary addresses in one request, and each one gets a calendar-invite email sent in the organizer's name, which turns this endpoint into a spam relay. HOW: Cap the array size (e.g. `.max(10)`), on top of rate limiting.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The blacklist entries are lowercased (line 71), but the incoming guest email is compared without normalisation, so `includes(guest)` misses any mixed-case version of a blacklisted address. An attacker can add a blacklisted guest by changing the case of a few letters (e.g. `Spam@Domain.com`). Lowercase the guest before the blacklist comparison.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: sendAddGuestsEmails in email-manager.ts assumes `newGuests` lists only newly added attendees and sends them the full AttendeeScheduledEmail invite. The handler instead passes the raw `guests` input, which can include emails that were already attendees. Those existing attendees then get a fresh booking confirmation instead of the add-guests notice; passing `uniqueGuests` fixes this.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Only the client dialog checks that guest emails are unique; the server schema accepts duplicates. The handler only removes guests who are already attendees, so a request like ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] creates two Attendee rows for the same email, because the Attendee table has no unique constraint. Enforce uniqueness on the server, for example by de-duplicating in the handler or adding a refine to the schema.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The handler filters the guests against an attendee list it read earlier, then calls createMany, with no transaction and no unique constraint on (bookingId, email). Two concurrent addGuests requests for the same booking can both pass the filter and insert the same guest twice. Re-check existing attendees inside a transaction, or add a unique constraint and use skipDuplicates.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`. Guests that were filtered out because they were already attendees still receive the new-booking (AttendeeScheduledEmail) email instead of the guests-added email.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner, but it is only true when the user passes both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner. A team admin who is not an owner therefore gets FORBIDDEN. Use || to match the intent.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The handler builds uniqueGuests by dropping existing attendees and blacklisted emails, but sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the original `guests`. Any existing attendee included in the input is treated as a new guest and gets a fresh 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notice. Pass uniqueGuests.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased, but each guest is compared exactly as entered. A blacklisted address typed with any uppercase letters gets past the filter. Lowercase the guest email before comparing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The booking is loaded with user.credentials, but EventManager is built from ctx.user and that user's own credentials. When an attendee or team admin adds guests, the update to the organizer's calendar event runs with the wrong user's credentials and will not find the event or will fail. Build EventManager from booking.user and its credentials.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The tooltip text "Remove email" is hard-coded in English. The rest of the component translates its text through t() from useLocale (for example t("add_another")), so users in other languages see this one string in English. Use a translation key instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner, but the code joins the isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner checks with &&, so it is only true when both pass. Code that trusts the name will assume admins without the owner role are allowed. Use || so the logic matches the name.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The message is built with a template literal that always contains text, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never uses the translated fallback. When err.data.code or err.message is missing, users see raw text like "undefined: " instead of the localized error.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment "These are like 40kb" appears to be copied from the phone input lazy loader. MultiEmail only uses existing UI components, so the size claim misleads readers about why it is lazy-loaded.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParse result object, and that object is written directly as credential.key. WHY: the DB key becomes {success, data}, so googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) at line 75 throws for every later request and the Google credential becomes unusable after the first refresh. HOW: store the parsed data.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: when credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this code reads res?.data as if it were a Gaxios response. WHY: token is undefined, so token.access_token throws a TypeError and Google tokens can never be refreshed in sync mode. HOW: in the sync branch, parse the Response JSON before using it, or make refreshOAuthTokens return the same shape that each caller expects.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: credentialId is passed where refreshOAuthTokens expects the credential's userId. WHY: the sync endpoint receives a credential id as calcomUserId, so it returns tokens for the wrong user or for none. HOW: pass the credential's userId instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: in sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this code reads tokenInfo.data.error as if it were an axios response. WHY: tokenInfo.data is undefined, so the property access throws and the token refresh always fails when sync is enabled. HOW: await the Response's json() in the sync branch and use that value as the token data.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: both computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to the literal property name '[object Object]', so the schema only declares access_token plus a field named '[object Object]'. WHY: zod strips every other field (expires_in, expiry_date, scope, token_type), so sync-mode refreshes lose expiry information and callers such as Zoom (expires_in) and office365 get NaN or missing values. HOW: use z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough(), with explicit optional expiry fields if needed.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: when the parsed response has no refresh_token, the code writes the literal string "refresh_token" into it. WHY: office365calendar spreads tokenResponse.data over the stored credentials (line 264), so a provider response without refresh_token (always the case with the stripping minimum schema) replaces the real stored refresh token with the string 'refresh_token', and the next refresh fails. HOW: remove the placeholder assignment so callers keep their existing refresh_token.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the new code calls prisma.credential.update, but the file never imports prisma. Imports at lines 1-20 have no @calcom/prisma. WHY: this causes a TypeScript compile error or a ReferenceError at runtime, which rejects getClient so every Salesforce operation fails. HOW: add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: success is detected by comparing response.statusText to "OK". WHY: statusText is empty over HTTP/2 and in many fetch implementations, so successful refreshes throw a 400 and the Salesforce client can never be created. HOW: check response.ok instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the token is refreshed and saved, but jsforce.Connection is still built with the old credentialKey.access_token and instance_url. WHY: the refresh result is discarded for the current connection, so requests use the stale or expired token. HOW: pass accessTokenParsed.data.access_token and accessTokenParsed.data.instance_url to the Connection.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: getClient runs on every SalesforceCalendarService construction and always makes a token refresh HTTP call plus a credential DB write, without checking whether the token is expired. WHY: this adds an external round-trip and a DB write to every booking or calendar operation, and frequent refreshes can hit Salesforce rate limits. HOW: refresh only when the token is invalid or expired, or rely on jsforce's built-in refresh handling.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: appStoreMetadata is indexed by app.slug, but the map is keyed by app directory name (see _appRegistry.ts:17, which uses app.dirName). WHY: for apps whose slug differs from their dirName (e.g. google-calendar vs googlecalendar), the lookup returns undefined and the webhook always responds 404, so those credentials cannot be synced. HOW: select dirName from prisma.app and index appStoreMetadata by it.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the webhook secret is checked with a plain !== string comparison. WHY: this endpoint can overwrite any user's third-party credentials, and a non-constant-time comparison exposes the secret to timing analysis. HOW: compare using crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers after confirming the header is a string.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: when state.teamId is present, the code only checks that the user is an accepted team member before creating a team credential, and throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam runs only on the path where teamId is falsy, so it is effectively a no-op. WHY: any non-admin team member can install OAuth apps on behalf of the team through a crafted state parameter. HOW: call throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam({ teamId: state.teamId, userId }) inside the teamId branch before prisma.credential.create.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: in sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the result is used directly as a HubspotToken. WHY: expiresIn and accessToken are undefined on a Response, so expiryDate becomes NaN, a Response object is persisted as the credential key, and setAccessToken(undefined) is called. HOW: parse the Response JSON in the sync branch before treating it as a token.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The webhook secret is checked with `!==`, which can leak timing information and let an attacker recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET byte by byte. Anyone with the secret can overwrite any user's app credentials. Compare in constant time with crypto.timingSafeEqual, after confirming the header is a string and the lengths match.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: `refreshOAuthTokens` gets `credentialId` (the Credential row id) as its `userId` argument. With credential sync enabled, it asks the sync endpoint for the tokens of the user whose id equals that credential id and saves them onto this credential. As a result, one user's Zoho Bigin access token is stored under another user's account and can be used by them; pass the credential owner's userId instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParseReturn ({success, data}), but this code saves that whole object as credential.key. The stored Google credential then holds {success, data} instead of access_token/refresh_token/expiry_date, which breaks later reads. Persist `.data` instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens declares its third parameter as userId and sends it to the sync endpoint as calcomUserId. This call passes credentialId instead, so in sync mode the endpoint is asked for tokens for the wrong (or a nonexistent) user. Pass the credential's userId instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but this code reads `res?.data` as if it were a googleapis response. That makes `token` undefined, so reading `token.access_token` throws and the refresh fails every time in sync mode. Parse the body with `await res.json()` when the sync path is used.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comments say any numeric property is treated as the expiry and that other properties are allowed. In fact `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the literal key "[object Object]", so both lines define that one key and the second overrides the first. Neither documented behaviour exists, so the schema validates a meaningless key instead of an expiry field and does not explicitly pass through extra fields.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens's third parameter is `userId` and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`, but here it receives the credential id. The sync endpoint is therefore told a credential id is a Cal.com user id, which looks up the wrong user (or none) and also bypasses the user-ownership check. Pass the credential's userId instead, for example by giving it to refreshAccessToken.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the result of `safeParse` (`{success, data}`), not the parsed credentials. Before this change, `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the plain credential object. Now `prisma.credential.update` stores `{success: true, data: {...}}` as the key, so the next read of `access_token` or `refresh_token` from the key finds nothing and authentication breaks.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `refreshOAuthTokens` sends its third argument to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`. When credential sync is enabled, the endpoint gets tokens for an unrelated user, or for no user, and those tokens are used for this credential.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When sync is enabled, this returns a fetch `Response`. The HubSpot, Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin callers expect a parsed token object or an axios response and read fields like `.data.error`. On a `Response`, `.data` is undefined, so `.data.error` throws a TypeError and the token refresh fails every time sync is on.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `googleCredentialSchema.parse()` used to return the key object, but `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a SafeParse result (`{ success, data }`). That whole wrapper now gets saved as `credential.key`. On the next read, `googleCredentialSchema` and `getGoogleAuth` won't find `access_token` or `refresh_token` at the top level, so every Google credential breaks after its first refresh. Store `.data` instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The third parameter of `refreshOAuthTokens` is the Cal.com `userId`, which the sync endpoint receives as `calcomUserId`. This consumer passes `credentialId`, so the parent app is asked for tokens belonging to the wrong user, or to a user that doesn't exist. Pass the credential's `userId` (it needs to be threaded through from `credential.userId`).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When credential sync is enabled, this function returns a fetch `Response`. The google, zoho-bigin and zohocrm callers still read `res.data` / `tokenInfo.data`, which is undefined on a `Response`, so the token refresh throws a TypeError whenever sync is on. Either have the sync path return the shape each caller expects, or update those callers to call `await response.json()`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The zoho-bigin change passes `credentialId` where a user id is expected. The reviewer flagged this as outside the assigned scope.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The Google Calendar change stores the whole `safeParse` result object as the credential key instead of only the parsed data. The reviewer flagged this as outside the assigned scope.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The computed keys in the zod schema (`[z.string().toString()]`) do not do what the comments describe. The reviewer flagged this as outside the assigned scope.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: In `createOAuthAppCredential`, the team branch checks only team membership and not admin access. The reviewer flagged this as outside the assigned scope.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParseReturn object (`{success, data}`), not the parsed credentials. That whole wrapper is written to `credential.key`, so the stored key no longer has access_token/refresh_token at the top level. Later reads of the credential then fail. Store `.data` instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens takes a userId as its third argument and sends it to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. Here it gets `credentialId` (credential.id), so the external app is asked for tokens for the wrong user. The guard also fires for team credentials, which other callers exclude by passing userId=null.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both become the same literal key, "[object Object]", so the second overwrites the first and the number/expiry rule is never applied. Because z.object strips unknown keys, the parsed data drops expiry and every other field except access_token. In sync mode this loses the expiry date. Use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response instead of the gaxios result. That Response has no `.data` property, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws. Because of this, Google token refresh always fails in sync mode. Parse the Response body as JSON in that branch.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The `retryCount > 1` branch of the deleteMany OR has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so the SMS cron deletes any WorkflowReminder (email or WhatsApp) whose retryCount is above 1. WHY: Once another cron starts incrementing retryCount, this job will silently delete reminders for other methods. HOW: Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the retryCount condition.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new retryCount increment sits inside `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)`, so a reminder with a missing phone number or an empty message never increments its counter. WHY: These reminders can never succeed, but they are still re-fetched and re-processed on every cron run until scheduledDate passes, which is the behavior the PR is meant to stop. HOW: Move the increment into an else branch of the outer `if` as well, or into one failure path that covers both cases.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The prisma.workflowReminder.update added in the catch block has no guard, so if it throws (for example P2025 because the reminder was deleted, or a DB error), the exception escapes the for-loop. WHY: All remaining reminders in this cron run are skipped and the handler returns an error instead of continuing. HOW: Wrap the catch-block update in its own try/catch, or use updateMany, which does not throw when no row matches.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Every failure from twilio.scheduleSMS increments retryCount, including temporary ones: an undefined return while the account is SMS-locked, a throw from checkSMSRateLimit when the monthly limit is hit, and Twilio network or 5xx errors. WHY: Two consecutive cron runs with a temporary failure permanently delete a valid reminder, so the attendee never gets the SMS even after the condition clears. HOW: Increment retryCount only for permanent errors, such as Twilio invalid-number error codes, and let temporary errors retry without counting.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: retryCount is written as `reminder.retryCount + 1` from a value read earlier, not with an atomic increment. WHY: Overlapping cron invocations processing the same reminder overwrite each other and lose increments. HOW: Use `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment says only past-dated SMS reminders are deleted, but the new OR branch also deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1, whatever its method or scheduled date. Update the comment so it describes both deletion criteria and readers aren't misled about which reminders are removed.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `retryCount > 1` branch of the OR has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so this SMS cron will delete any WorkflowReminder (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, ...) whose retryCount exceeds 1. The comment and the rest of the handler are scoped to SMS, but this clause isn't. Add the method filter inside this branch so the cleanup only touches SMS reminders.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Before this change, the per-reminder catch block only logged, so one bad reminder never stopped the cron run. It now awaits `prisma.workflowReminder.update` without a guard, so if that update throws (DB error, or the record was deleted at the same time), the exception escapes the loop. The handler then fails and all remaining reminders in this run go unscheduled.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new update in the catch block can throw. That happens if the reminder was deleted concurrently (for example, its booking was cancelled), which gives P2025, or if the original error was a DB failure. The throw escapes the for loop, so every remaining reminder is skipped and the handler returns a 500 instead of carrying on. Use updateMany, which does not throw when no row matches, and catch any error from it so one failed reminder cannot stop the batch.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The second OR branch deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, whatever its method. This SMS cron can therefore delete EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders as soon as any other path starts using retryCount. Add method: WorkflowMethods.SMS to this branch.

suggestions.label: possible_issue
suggestions.suggestionContent: The retryCount branch of the OR condition in the cleanup is not limited to SMS reminders, so it may delete or affect non-SMS reminders. The reviewer flagged this as outside their assigned review class.

suggestions.label: possible_issue
suggestions.suggestionContent: The retry counter is updated with a read-then-write instead of an atomic increment. Concurrent runs could lose updates. The reviewer flagged this as outside their assigned review class.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new backup-code branch is evaluated even when the password check was skipped. The existing guard `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` skips verifyPassword whenever totpCode is non-empty, and the backup-code branch then ignores totpCode entirely. WHY: An attacker who has a victim's email and one leaked backup code can POST credentials with `totpCode=x` and `backupCode=<code>` and log in without the password, so the backup code replaces both factors. HOW: Require that the password was verified before accepting a backup code. For example, reject when `credentials.backupCode` is set and the password check did not run, or run verifyPassword unconditionally in the backup-code branch.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Spending a backup code is a non-atomic read-decrypt-modify-write of `user.backupCodes`, with no lock and no condition that the stored value is unchanged. WHY: Two concurrent login requests with the same code both read the old list, both find the code, and both succeed, so a single-use code can authenticate multiple sessions. HOW: Make the update conditional on the previously read ciphertext (`updateMany({ where: { id: user.id, backupCodes: user.backupCodes }, ... })`) and reject the login if count is 0.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: 2FA is already enabled on the server when the DisplayBackupCodes step is shown, but onEnable() and resetState() run only from the Close button; dismissing the dialog with Escape or an overlay click goes through the parent's onOpenChange, which just toggles `enableModalOpen`. WHY: After that dismissal, viewer.me is never invalidated, so the switch stays unchecked even though 2FA is on. The next time the modal opens it starts on the stale backup-codes step instead of ConfirmPassword. HOW: Wrap onOpenChange so that closing while `step === SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` calls resetState() and onEnable().

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex (`randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`), but the user's input is compared exactly after stripping only dashes, with no case normalization. WHY: A user who types the code in uppercase, which the 'XXXXX-XXXXX' placeholder invites, gets IncorrectBackupCode and can be locked out of recovery. HOW: Normalize with `.toLowerCase()` before indexOf.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new backup-code input component is declared as `function TwoFactor`, a name copied from the TOTP component, so stack traces and React DevTools will show TwoFactor for a different component. Rename it to BackupCode so the name matches the file and what the component does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This error message was copied from the login flow and says "cannot proceed with backup code login", but this endpoint disables 2FA. Anyone reading the logs would be pointed to the wrong flow. Change the wording to describe disabling 2FA.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The code reads the backup-code list, checks it in memory, then writes it back with an unconditional update. Two concurrent logins can both read the old list, so the same one-time code is accepted twice, and concurrent use of different codes can bring an already-used code back to life. Make the write conditional on the ciphertext that was read (for example `updateMany` where `backupCodes` still equals the value read, and reject the login if the update count is 0), or run it in a serializable transaction.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The backup code typed by the user is checked against the stored codes with `backupCodes.indexOf(...)`, which uses ordinary string equality. That comparison can stop at the first mismatched character and run faster or slower depending on the input, so response timing can leak information about the stored codes. Compare each stored code with crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers instead (the same check is used in disable.ts).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `isChecked()` returns a Promise that is never awaited, so `toBeTruthy()` always passes, even when 2FA is not enabled. After this PR, the modal stays on the backup-codes step until Close is clicked, so the switch is still unchecked at this point and the test passes anyway. Click `backup-codes-close` first, then assert on `data-state="checked"`, as the second test does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The success toast is shown right after `navigator.clipboard.writeText` is called, without waiting for the copy to succeed, so waiting for the toast proves nothing about the copy. The test would still pass if the copied text were wrong or the clipboard write failed. Read the clipboard and check that it contains the 10 formatted backup codes.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a non-null `Prisma.Sql`, even when access is denied (it returns `NOTHING_CONDITION`), and a Sql object is always truthy. So the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches can never run. Anyone reading the code would wrongly think filters might be applied without authorization; simplify to always using `authConditions`, ANDed with `filterConditions` when that is present.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The only booking in this test matches both the authorization condition (the user's own non-team booking) and the eventTypeId filter. As a result, getBaseConditions would still pass if it returned only authConditions, only filterConditions, or joined them with OR. Add a booking for the same user with a different event type, which the filter should exclude, and a booking of the filtered event type that auth should exclude (for example, by another user). Then assert that only userBooking is returned.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged for raw_html posts, so HTML imported from RSS (after CGI.unescapeHTML) or from remote pages is stored as `cooked` with no sanitization. WHY: <script> tags, event handlers or `javascript:` hrefs in feed or page content run in the Discourse origin wherever cooked is rendered (topic view and the embed iframe use `raw post.cooked`), which is stored XSS. HOW: run the raw HTML through the same whitelist sanitizer the normal pipeline uses (e.g. PrettyText's sanitize step) before returning it.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `url` is interpolated into `#{url}` without HTML escaping, and it comes from the user-supplied embed_url parameter (TopicRetriever only checks the host). WHY: a URL like `http://host/'onmouseover='alert(1)` is a valid URI and breaks out of the attribute, injecting an event handler into the imported post. HOW: escape the URL with ERB::Util.html_escape in both the attribute and the link text.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The throttle key is the full embed URL, and anonymous requests to /embed/best (whose Referer can be forged by non-browser clients) enqueue retrieve jobs that create topics. WHY: an attacker can vary the query string or path on the embeddable host (`?a=1`, `?a=2`, ...) to get past the throttle and make the server create an unlimited number of topics as embed_by_username. HOW: throttle per client or globally rather than per URL, and normalize the URL (or drop the query string) before using it as the throttle key and embed key.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: For every embed URL that is not yet imported, perform_retrieve runs Jobs::PollFeed synchronously, which downloads the whole feed and runs TopicEmbed.import for every item. WHY: every retrieval for an unknown URL (which an anonymous caller can trigger repeatedly with distinct URLs) costs a full feed fetch with no timeout plus N import/SHA comparisons, so worker time grows with feed size × request rate. HOW: rely on the hourly scheduled poll, or cache the last poll time in Redis and skip the inline poll if one ran recently.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `href.start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/a.png`, and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes. WHY: external links and images become `http://host/cdn.example.com/a.png`, which breaks them in every imported post. HOW: skip values that start with `//` (and do the same for img src).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `i.content.scrub` assumes every feed item has a <content> element, but standard RSS 2.0 items often only have <description>, in which case SimpleRSS returns nil for content. WHY: the NoMethodError on nil aborts the whole poll (retry: false) and also aborts the inline poll inside TopicRetriever, so no items are imported. HOW: fall back to description and skip items that have no body.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `post = embed.post` can be nil when the imported post has been deleted (soft-deleted posts are excluded by the default scope), and it is passed straight to PostRevisor. WHY: when the feed content changes, `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError, which aborts the feed poll for every remaining item. HOW: return early (or recreate the post) when embed.post is nil.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `<%- end if %>` leaves a dangling `if` modifier, so the next compiled template expression (the logo output) becomes the condition of the whole if/else block. WHY: the logo is written to the buffer before the header button, so the header renders in the wrong order. HOW: use a plain `<%- end %>`.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` accepts any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl. For example, `https://forum.example.co` passes for `https://forum.example.com/`, so an attacker-controlled domain can send messages to the embedding page. Parse discourseUrl and compare its exact origin to `e.origin` instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The embed view formats dates with strftime("%e %b %Y"), which always gives English month abbreviations and a fixed day-month-year order. Every other string in this view goes through I18n.t, so this date is the one piece of text that is not localised. Use I18n.l with a date format instead.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The imported_from footer builds `#{url}` from a feed-supplied URL without escaping it. The post is cooked as raw_html, so this markup is shown to readers unchanged. A quote or `<` in the URL breaks out of the attribute and injects markup. Escape the URL with ERB::Util.html_escape before putting it into the HTML.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: SimpleRSS sets `content` only from a `<content>` element; standard RSS 2.0 items only have `<description>`, so `i.content` is nil and `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError. The error aborts the whole poll, so no items get imported, and it also propagates into TopicRetriever, which runs PollFeed synchronously. Fall back to `description` (or skip the item) when `content` is nil.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The code looks up `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then creates the topic, post and embed, with no lock between the two steps. PollFeed, RetrieveTopic jobs (staff skip the throttle) and the Disqus importer can import the same URL at the same time. Both see no embed, and the second `create!` raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique on the unique `embed_url` index, which crashes that job and stops the rest of its feed loop. Rescue RecordNotUnique and fall back to the update path, or serialize imports per URL with a lock.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `start_with?('/')` also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png`, and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, giving `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/img.png`. Imported links and images that point to other hosts therefore break. Skip values that start with `//` in both the `a` loop and the `img` loop.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: `indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that appears anywhere in discourseUrl, including a shorter host that is a prefix, like `http://forum.example.co` for `http://forum.example.com/`. Messages from that origin are then trusted and can resize the iframe. Require discourseUrl to begin with the exact origin followed by `/`, or to equal it.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: `best` builds the TopicView for `current_user`, so a staff member or a user with extra permissions may see posts that anonymous visitors cannot. It then calls `discourse_expires_in 1.minute`, and if that marks the response publicly cacheable, a shared proxy or CDN can serve that version to other visitors of the embedding page for up to a minute. Render the embed as anonymous (pass `nil` as the user) or skip public caching when a user is logged in.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This test only sets feed_polling_url to nil. feed_polling_enabled? stays false by default and embed_by_username stays blank, so poll_feed is never called whether or not the url check exists. Stub feed_polling_enabled? to true and embed_by_username to a real name so the url check is the only thing stopping the call.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This test only sets embed_by_username to nil. feed_polling_enabled? is still false and feed_polling_url is still blank by default, so execute never calls poll_feed whether or not the username check exists. Stub the other two settings to valid values so the username check is the only thing stopping the call.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: feed_polling_url and embed_by_username are blank by default, so the present? checks alone keep poll_feed from being called. The test would still pass if the feed_polling_enabled? check were deleted. Stub the url and username to valid values so only the enabled flag is false.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `execute(...)[0]['id']` (and `[0]['value']` on line 15) assumes the query returns a row. On sites where embed_category is unset or does not match a category name, or where uncategorized_category_id is not stored in site_settings, it returns none. WHY: `[0]` is nil, so the migration raises NoMethodError and the deploy fails. HOW: Check the result's ntuples before indexing and fall back to a default.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Legacy embeddable_hosts values (often 'http://host', with paths or trailing \r) are inserted raw, skipping the model's scheme/path stripping. WHY: EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares the column against the bare uri.host, so migrated entries like 'http://discourse.org' never match, and embedding stops working for existing sites after upgrade. HOW: Before inserting, strip whitespace, the scheme and any path from each value.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Host values from site_settings are interpolated directly into an INSERT statement as '#{h}'. WHY: A value containing a single quote breaks the migration or injects arbitrary SQL that runs with migration privileges. HOW: Quote the value with connection.quote(h).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The query lowercases the column (`lower(host)`) but compares it to uri.host without downcasing it. WHY: A referer or embed URL with uppercase characters (e.g. 'http://EvilTrout.com/x') fails the check, and embedding is wrongly rejected. HOW: Downcase the argument.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The validation regex accepts a port and before_validation keeps it in the stored host ('example.com:8080'), but record_for_host compares against uri.host, which never includes the port. WHY: Hosts saved with a port pass validation and can never match a referer, so embedding from them always fails. HOW: Either compare host plus port (when it is not the default port), or strip the port before saving.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: before_validation calls `self.host.sub!` with no nil guard. WHY: A create/update request without a host param (or EmbeddableHost.new without a host) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. HOW: Return early when host is nil.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: destroy (and update) use `where(id:).first`, which returns nil for an unknown id, and then call methods on it. WHY: Deleting or updating a host that does not exist (or was already deleted) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404. HOW: Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` so ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound returns a 404.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The new `_ids` branch runs for every key ending in `_ids` on every hydrated model. It always deletes the original key and replaces it with the result of mapping _lookupSubType, which returns undefined when the root has no matching collection; a null value crashes on `.map`. WHY: Existing REST models with plain id-array attributes (e.g. `group_ids`) lose that data or throw while hydrating, a regression outside the embedding feature. HOW: Only replace the key when the value is an array and the pluralized collection exists in root.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `record_for_host` lowercases the stored `host` column but compares it with `uri.host` unchanged, and Ruby's URI does not lowercase hostnames. A referer like `http://EvilTrout.com/page` therefore never matches an allowed host, so embed checks and topic retrieval reject valid hosts. Fix: lowercase the incoming host (`host.downcase`) so both sides are normalised the same way.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains every category fabricator. Each file name now describes the other file's contents, so anyone looking for a fabricator by file name opens the wrong file. Swap the contents back so each file holds the fabricator it is named after.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This change removed the embeddable-host check from `expandable_first_post?`, but the test is still called "is false if embeddable_host is blank". It actually passes because the newly built topic has no topic embed, so the name points readers to a condition the code no longer checks. Rename it to describe the real reason it returns false.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: expandable_first_post? no longer checks embeddable hosts. This test returns false only because the built topic has no topic embed (has_topic_embed? is false), so the name claims behaviour the code does not have. It would pass whether or not any host exists, so either rename it to match what it really covers or remove it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration assumes the `embed_category` join query returns at least one row. Site settings left at their default are not stored in `site_settings`, so on most installs the result is empty and `[0]['id']` raises, aborting the migration. Check the row count before indexing and fall back to the uncategorized category if there are no rows.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The validation accepts `host:port`, and before_validation strips only the scheme and path, so a value like `example.com:8080` is stored with its port. `record_for_host` compares that column against `uri.host`, which never includes the port, so the record is unreachable and embedding from that host is always rejected. Either strip the port before saving or compare against host plus port.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `lower(host) = ?` lowercases only the stored value, while `uri.host` keeps the referer's original case. A referer like `http://EvilTrout.com` therefore never matches the stored `eviltrout.com`. Downcase the referer host before comparing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The query compares `lower(host)` with `uri.host`, but Ruby's URI keeps the original case, so a referer like `http://EvilTrout.com/page` will never match the stored host. Embeds and topic retrieval then wrongly fail with 'invalid referer host'. Lowercase the input before comparing.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: If `embed_category` is unset or names no existing category, the SELECT returns no rows. `[0]` is then nil and `['id']` raises NoMethodError, so the migration aborts and the `category_id == 0` fallback can never run. Guard against an empty result before reading the id.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The validation regex allows `:port`, and `before_validation` only strips the scheme and path, so `example.com:8080` is saved with the port. `record_for_host` compares against `uri.host`, which never includes a port, so such hosts can never be allowed. Strip the port before saving, or include `uri.port` when looking up.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When no 'embed_category' row exists in site_settings (the default, since defaults aren't stored), the SELECT returns zero rows. `[0]` is then nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, which aborts the migration on most installs.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The before_validation callback calls `sub!` on `host` with no nil check. Creating or updating a host without a host value (for example when `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is missing) raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `where(...).first` returns nil for an unknown id (for example a double delete or a stale UI), and `host.destroy` then raises NoMethodError, which returns a 500. Use `find` so the request returns a 404 instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Any payload key ending in `_ids` whose value is null now reaches `obj[k].map`, which throws a TypeError. Before this change such keys were only matched by the `_id` regex and handled safely, so hydrating the record now fails.

suggestions.label: possible bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Possible issue: `record_for_host` compares the database's `lower(host)` against `uri.host`, which isn't lowercased, so a referer containing capital letters would fail the host-allowed check. Lowercase `uri.host` before comparing. (The reviewer noted this as outside the cross-file assignment, since it sits within a single hunk, and did not formally report it.)

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently replaces the 5-argument `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, because Ruby has no overloading. WHY: `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` (app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14) still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`, which now raises ArgumentError (5 for 3..4), so emoji resizing breaks. HOW: Merge them into one method that accepts both forms, e.g. `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions_or_width, max_height=nil, opts={})`, or give the new variant a different name.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: For GIFs with allow_animated_thumbnails enabled, "80%" is passed to downsize_instructions_animated, which runs `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`; gifsicle expects WxH there, not a percentage. WHY: gifsicle fails, convert_with returns false, the file never shrinks, and all 5 attempts are wasted before the oversized GIF is rejected anyway. HOW: For animated GIFs, compute explicit pixel dimensions (80% of the current width and height) instead of passing a percentage.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: tempfile.path is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize, and convert_with runs it in a shell through backticks without escaping. For API URL uploads, that path contains the request-controlled `type` param (`discourse-upload-#{type}`). WHY: A `type` containing shell metacharacters such as `$(...)` or `;` runs arbitrary commands on the server when the oversized image is downsized. HOW: Restrict `type` to a whitelist (or Shellwords-escape every argument in convert_with) before the path reaches the shell.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Any image up to 10MB is now run through ImageMagick `convert` up to 5 times in the upload path, with no limit on pixel dimensions. WHY: A small, highly compressed image with huge pixel dimensions (a decompression bomb) makes each convert run allocate gigabytes and burn CPU, which ties up web/defer workers. HOW: Check pixel dimensions (e.g. FastImage.size) before downsizing and reject images above a sane limit.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The client-side size check now uses a hardcoded 10MB for every upload type, attachments included, instead of `max_<type>_size_kb`. WHY: Sites with max_attachment_size_kb above 10MB now see larger attachments rejected in the browser, and the error message reports the wrong limit for attachments. HOW: Keep the hardcoded 10MB only for images and keep using the site setting for other types.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Ruby has no method overloading, so the second `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` version. `ResizeEmoji` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 arguments and now gets an ArgumentError, so emoji resizing breaks. Use one method that accepts both forms, or give the dimensions-string variant a different name.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Ruby has no overloading, so `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition just above it. app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 arguments, which now raises ArgumentError, so emoji resizing breaks. Merge the two into one method that accepts both forms, or update the emoji job to pass "100x100".

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Ruby keeps only the last `def self.downsize`, so the `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` version is silently overwritten by `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. The existing call in app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 (`OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`) now raises ArgumentError (5 for 3..4), so emoji resizing breaks. Combine the two into one method that accepts both call styles, or give the new one a different name.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The client size check now uses a fixed 10MB limit for every upload type, including attachments, instead of `max_attachment_size_kb`. If that setting is above 10MB, the browser rejects attachments the server would accept. Only image uploads, which the server can now shrink, should get the larger client-side limit.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new 3-argument `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` was added so uploads_controller can pass "80%", but Ruby has no overloading, so it replaces the 4-argument `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` defined just above it. As a result, `ResizeEmoji` (`OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`) now raises ArgumentError because it passes 5 arguments to a method that accepts 3–4. Keep one `downsize` that accepts both call shapes, or give the new form a different name and use that name in the controller.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The size check and the `file_too_large` message now use a hard-coded 10MB for every upload type. The server still enforces `max_attachment_size_kb` for attachments (site_settings.yml:516). So users see a max size that doesn't match the limit actually applied, and an attachment the client accepts can still be rejected by the server. Keep using `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` for attachments, and only raise the client limit for images, which the server now downsizes.

suggestions.label: bug

HOW: Check that the device exists with a SELECT on device_id within the window instead of relying on RowsAffected.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts devices and then inserts without a transaction, lock or constraint. WHY: Concurrent requests from new devices can all see count < deviceLimit before any of them inserts, so the configured limit is exceeded. HOW: Run the count and insert in one transaction with appropriate locking, or do a conditional insert that checks the count in the same statement.

suggestions.label: performance
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Device tagging used to run in a background goroutine with its own timeout and now runs inline in Authenticate. WHY: Anonymous authentication now waits on these DB round trips, so a slow DB or a flood of new device IDs adds latency and DB load to every such anonymous request. HOW: Keep the DB write async and enforce the limit from a cached or periodically refreshed device count.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The doc comment says `updateDevice` updates a device "updated between the given times", but it takes only ctx and device. It computes the window internally as `device.UpdatedAt` minus 30 days to `device.UpdatedAt` plus one minute, and returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when no row matches, so callers reading the comment get the wrong contract.

suggestions.label: bug

Every goroutine that saw a nil cache under the RLock therefore re-reads and re-parses the manifest and overwrites the cache, even after another goroutine has already filled it. Re-check the cache right after taking the write lock (outside Dev) and return it if it is set.

suggestions.label: bug

If a later reload fails, it overwrites the good cached value with nil and that caller gets an error. suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The flusher processes are SpawnProcess instances (from get_context('spawn').Process), and SpawnProcess subclasses BaseProcess rather than multiprocessing.Process, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False and kill() is never called. WHY: Every submit now sends N times as many INFO requests across the cluster, and the totals are just duplicated (the ratio does not change). HOW: Query memory info once, through any single buffer.

suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When the join deadline runs out, the loop `break`s, and terminate() is never called on the processes it has not visited yet. WHY: Those flusher processes can keep running after join returns and may keep flushing shards that have already been reassigned during a rebalance. HOW: Instead of breaking, skip the wait but still terminate each remaining process.

WHY: The flusher threads still race against step.join(), which sets stopped, so `(msg,) = messages` can fail intermittently. HOW: Poll until messages is non-empty (with a bounded loop) before calling join.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The docstring says the flusher creates one process per shard. In the code, the process count is min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards)) and shards are spread round-robin, so one process can serve several shards. With the CLI default of --flusher-processes=1, all shards share a single process.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Every other flusher metric added in this change tags with "shard", but spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce uses "shards". Anyone filtering or grouping by the "shard" tag will silently miss this metric.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The test only checks that the shard counts across processes add up to 4. That stays true if the round-robin mapping is broken and puts every shard in one process, leaving the others empty. Assert the exact mapping (e.g. `{0: [0, 2], 1: [1, 3]}`) or at least that every process gets a non-empty shard list.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `time.sleep` is patched to `lambda _: None` at the top of test_basic, so the `time.sleep(0.1)` meant to give the flusher threads time to process returns immediately. The test synchronises on nothing. Wait on a condition instead, e.g. poll until `messages` is non-empty with a bounded loop.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Restarting a flusher used to always kill the old process, but now it only kills if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. That check is always false for the SpawnProcess objects created by mp_context.Process, because SpawnProcess derives from BaseProcess. So a process that hangs keeps running next to its replacement, and both write the same healthy_since/backpressure Values and flush the same shards.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When the deadline has passed, join() hits `break` before it calls `terminate()` on the processes that come later in `self.processes`. Those flusher processes keep running after join() returns. When the deadline expires, skip the wait but still terminate every remaining process.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: These processes are SpawnProcess instances from get_context("spawn"), and SpawnProcess does not subclass multiprocessing.Process, so the isinstance check is always False and kill() is skipped. When a process hangs, a second flusher starts on the same shards while the first keeps running. Both drain the same Redis queues and update the same shared Values, which can produce duplicate segments and leaks a process on every restart. Check for threading.Thread instead (or use multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess) so real processes get killed.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The other per-shard flusher metrics in this change (`flusher.produce`, `segment_size_bytes`, `flusher_unhealthy`) use the tag key `shard`, but `wait_produce` uses `shards`. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The processes are created with `mp_context.Process` from a spawn context, so they are `SpawnProcess` instances. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so this check is always false and `kill()` never runs. A hung flusher therefore keeps running while a replacement is started on the same shards; check `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)` instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: When the deadline passes, the `break` leaves the loop before the remaining processes reach `process.terminate()`, so they are never stopped. The inner `while` already respects the deadline, so remove the early `break` and let every process reach the terminate step.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls inside it, checkIfIsAvailable returns true right away and never runs the busy check. WHY: Existing bookings and calendar busy times are ignored on override days, so already-booked slots are offered and can be double-booked. HOW: Remove the early return so the busy.every check still runs; use dateOverrideExist only to skip the working-hours check.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Two different Dayjs instances are compared with ===, which is reference equality and always false. WHY: A day-off override (start equals end) is never detected, so a slot starting exactly at the override time passes the later range checks and stays bookable. HOW: Use `.isSame()` to compare the two times.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The end-bound check uses slotStartTime.isAfter(override end) instead of checking the slot's end time. WHY: A slot that starts inside the override but runs past its end (e.g. a 60-minute slot at 10:30 for a 10:00-11:00 override) is accepted, so a host can be booked outside their override hours. HOW: Reject the slot when slotEndTime is after the override end.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The start-bound check only rejects slots that end at or before the override start; it never checks whether the slot starts before the override. WHY: A slot that begins before the override window and ends inside it is treated as available, so fixed hosts can be booked partly outside their override hours. HOW: Reject the slot when slotStartTime is before the override start.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `end` is computed from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, so it always equals `start`. WHY: Slots that start inside working hours but end after them (e.g. a 60-minute slot at 16:30 when work ends at 17:00) are not rejected. HOW: Compute `end` from slotEndTime.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The working-hours check marks a slot unavailable if ANY working-hours range on that weekday does not contain it. WHY: Users with split availability (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17 on the same day) have every slot rejected, because each slot falls outside at least one range, so no slots are offered at all. HOW: Mark the slot unavailable only when no range for that day contains it (use some/every over the ranges for that day).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: The override date is formatted with `dayjs(...)`, which uses the server's local timezone, while the slot date is formatted in UTC. WHY: On a server not running in UTC, the day comparison is off for overrides near midnight, so overrides get applied to the wrong day or skipped. HOW: Use dayjs.utc(date.start) before adding the offset and formatting.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: After the timezone offset is added, startTime/endTime are computed as hour*60+minute, which wraps at midnight. WHY: For overrides that cross the invitee's midnight (e.g. 20:00-23:00 UTC shown to a +6:00 invitee), endTime ends up smaller than startTime, so buildSlots produces no slots or slots in the wrong part of the day. HOW: Compute minutes relative to the start of the invitee's day (e.g. diff in minutes from startOfInviteeDay) instead of taking hour/minute of the shifted time.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `end` is named for, and compared against, the end of working hours, but it is calculated from `slotStartTime`, which makes it identical to `start`. As a result, `end > workingHour.endTime` never catches a slot that starts inside working hours and runs past their end. Compute it from `slotEndTime` so the value matches its name.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `end` is calculated from `slotStartTime`, so it always equals `start`, and the `end > workingHour.endTime` check never catches a slot that runs past closing time. Example: with working hours 9:00-17:00 and a 60-minute event, a 16:30 slot is accepted even though it ends at 17:30. Calculate `end` from `slotEndTime`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The end-side test only rejects slots whose start is strictly after the override end. A slot that starts exactly at the end, or that starts inside the override but runs past its end, is still treated as available. Example: with an override of 09:00-12:00 and a 60-minute event, slots at 11:30 and 12:00 are both accepted.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `end` is computed from slotStartTime, so it always equals `start`, and `end > workingHour.endTime` only fires when the slot starts after working hours end. Slots that start inside working hours but run past the end are wrongly treated as available. Compute `end` from slotEndTime.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `dayjs(...) === dayjs(...)` compares two different object references, so it is always false. A zero-length override (one that marks the day unavailable) is never caught by this branch. Use `.isSame()` to compare the instants.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `find` returns true, which makes the slot unavailable, as soon as the slot falls outside any single override on that date. With several override ranges on one day (e.g. 9-11 and 14-16), a 14:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the 9-11 range. The slot should be rejected only when it fits in none of that day's override ranges.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: This PR makes checkIfIsAvailable reject slots outside the user's date overrides and working hours. This call site looks up userSchedule but passes only its timeZone, so dateOverrides and workingHours fall back to []. Slots for this user are then checked only against busy times, unlike the other two call sites, which spread the user's schedule.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `dayjs(a) === dayjs(b)` compares two new object references, so it is always false. As a result, a date override that marks the day unavailable (start == end) is never rejected here. A slot starting exactly at the override's start passes both later checks and gets reported as available. Use `.isSame()` instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `end` is calculated from slotStartTime, the same value as `start`, so the `end > workingHour.endTime` check never looks at when the slot actually ends. A slot that starts inside working hours but runs past their end is therefore accepted. Calculate `end` from slotEndTime.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `workingHours.find` returns a match as soon as the slot falls outside ANY working-hour entry for that weekday. With split ranges on one day (e.g. 9–12 and 13–17), a 14:00 slot is outside 9–12 and gets rejected, even though 13–17 contains it. The slot should be rejected only when no entry for that day contains it.

suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Each `import()` in the appStore object literal runs as soon as the module loads, so all 28 app packages are fetched and evaluated immediately, and each one creates a promise with no rejection handler until some caller happens to await that key. WHY: Nothing is lazily loaded, so cold-start cost is unchanged. suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: After a successful cache delete, the component does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: When the credential is missing or not owned, the handler throws a plain `Error` instead of a `TRPCError`. WHY: tRPC maps it to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500), so an expected authorization or not-found case shows up as a server failure and is logged as one. HOW: Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND", message: ... })`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `sed -i '' -E ...` uses BSD/macOS in-place syntax. WHY: On GNU sed (Linux), `''` is read as the sed script and the real expression as a filename, so the command fails and GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated when the key already exists. HOW: Use a portable form such as `sed -i.bak -E "..." "$ENV_FILE" && rm -f "$ENV_FILE.bak"`.

suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment says this call refreshes `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, but it passes an empty `data` object. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes empty `data` and relies on Prisma's `@updatedAt` to touch the rows. Prisma may skip the update or leave `updatedAt` unchanged when `data` is empty, so the timestamp would go stale after every cache refresh. Set the timestamp explicitly so the write always happens.
